lane: BOOT (the opening film and the orb waking)

features.name: The 7-second opening film
features.where: Open Ghosty cold from the Home Screen (The Scan look, the default)
features.does: The eye opens, a scan sweeps over your desk and the city, the camera comes down from the sky, the things you use lock in, the orb forms, then the stamp, the feeds and the greeting, and it lands on Home at about 7 seconds
features.note: Fixed in the final round: before that it never played on the phone (it fell to a 1.7-second fallback every time)

features.name: The short cut after a quick reopen
features.where: Close Ghosty, then open it again within 3 minutes
features.does: The same shots, closer together, landing at about 4.8 seconds, so a quick return doesn't sit through the whole film
features.note: The 3-minute rule is fixed in code, not a setting

features.name: Tap to skip
features.does: Goes straight to the landing on Home, with no greeting after the tap

features.name: Calm version for Reduce Motion
features.where: iPhone Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Reduce Motion, or THE LOOK → Motion → calm
features.does: Two still frames, about a second, nothing travelling, with every word the full film has

features.name: The landing on Home
features.does: The orb lands exactly where Home's orb lives (the same orb, never a copy), and the bar and cards slide in a beat later

features.name: The greeting
features.where: In the film, under the stamp
features.does: 'Good evening, <your name>.' from the clock and the name in Settings, spoken in your voice when the voice setting is on (on iPhone, at your first tap)
features.note: With no name saved it says just 'Good evening.'

features.name: The stamp and the feeds in the film
features.where: In the film, at the top
features.does: Types the day, the time, your saved place and the feeds' state, then one true line for each feed that answered (flood, weather, crime counts from public sources)
features.note: Offline it says so in one line, with no made-up feeds

features.name: The boot's score
features.does: A short score made on the phone under the film (no sound files); off, just the one recognition tone
features.note: Silent on a cold open until your first tap, because iPhone insists

features.name: Replay from SYSTEM
features.where: SYSTEM → REBOOT HIM, or the command palette's 'Reboot him'
features.does: Plays the whole film again over Home

features.name: A breath on return
features.where: Switch away from Ghosty and back while it is still running
features.does: No film, just the orb breathing once

features.name: Slow-open honesty
features.where: A slow network or a cold brain at open
features.does: The film keeps moving and, after a second, says what it is waiting for (the brain or the signal), never a frozen frame

features.name: The boot's failure screen
features.does: 'I couldn't start this time. Tap to try again.' and the tap does it

features.name: The opening in the other six looks
features.where: THE LOOK → Map, Eye, One Ink, Glass, Orbit or Grown Up
features.does: A shorter 2.9-second opening in each look's own style (the Eye's ends with its wall resolving from grain)
features.note: Only The Scan has the 7-second film

features.name: The orb's five states
features.does: Idle, listening, thinking, speaking and attending, each with its own light and shape, readable even with motion off
features.note: Clearer than before, but the check that measures them is sensitive to the scene behind the orb and isn't reliably green

upward.why: The Map, The Eye, One Ink, Glass, Orbit and Grown Up would each open as richly as The Scan, in their own style
upward.builds_on: The film's conductor and its shot timing; the Eye's wall-from-grain shot

upward.idea: A film that knows the day
upward.why: The opening shows what matters today: the search locks on your first meeting, a bill due, or rain coming, instead of a fixed choice
upward.builds_on: The film's search shot, the Brief, the agenda and the weather feed

upward.idea: Seasons and time of day in the film
upward.why: Night opens on lit windows, morning on low sun, winter on frost, so the film never feels the same twice
upward.builds_on: The world lit by the hour, and the film's lighting

upward.idea: A choice of opening length in Settings
upward.why: Full film always, the short cut always, or the film only once a day, so you choose your own rhythm
upward.builds_on: The full, short and quick-reopen rules

upward.why: The day's first open shows a fuller film with the day's one line ('Three things today'); later opens are shorter
upward.builds_on: The 'when you were last here' stamp and the Brief

upward.why: A soft tap on the phone as the orb locks in and the greeting lands, so it feels like a premium device waking
upward.builds_on: The film's phase moments and the recognition tone

upward.idea: A richer score with your colour's key
upward.why: The music changes key and texture with your chosen colour and the time of day, still made on the phone
'Welcome back, it's been three days' or 'Good morning, the Brief is ready', only from your own data
upward.builds_on: The greeting and the 'when you were last here' stamp

upward.idea: An on-phone frame-rate readout for the film
upward.why: After an open you can see how smoothly it ran on your phone (frames, any stutter), so problems are caught at once
upward.builds_on: The film's frame budget, which is already measured

upward.idea: Starting the app faster under the film
upward.why: Moving non-urgent start-up work until after the landing makes the first second smoother and Home ready sooner

upward.idea: The orb's states said once in words
upward.why: The first time it listens or thinks, a short line explains what the light means, so anyone can read the orb
upward.builds_on: The orb's five states and the hint system

upward.why: Step through the film shot by shot with each shot named, to show it off or to fine-tune it
upward.builds_on: The film's manual step-through, which the checks already use

sideways.why: Saying 'goodnight' plays a 3-second wind-down (the feeds dim, the orb rests) and switches the night ground on
sideways.builds_on: The film's shots run in reverse, and the night ground

sideways.why: Short 2-second films for big moments: a course finished, a budget hit, a game won, a comic completed
sideways.builds_on: The film's recognition wave and score

sideways.why: Record your own opening as a short video to keep, posted only with APPROVE
sideways.builds_on: The film, and the video editor's export

sideways.why: A big-screen version of the film when Ghosty is cast to the television, tuned for distance
sideways.builds_on: TV mode's short cut and the film

sideways.idea: An opening for a home-screen widget
sideways.why: The widget wakes with a tiny version of the orb's lock-in when it refreshes
sideways.builds_on: The orb and the widget host

sideways.why: When focus or study mode is on, the opening is a single quiet breath and goes straight to the task
sideways.builds_on: The still version and the modes

sideways.why: When you hand the phone to someone you introduced, the opening greets them by name, never anyone unknown
sideways.builds_on: The greeting and the people you introduce

sideways.idea: A replayable film of your day
sideways.why: In the evening, a 10-second film flies over today's places and things from your own records
sideways.builds_on: The film's descent camera, the map and the agenda; the brain never gets live GPS

sideways.why: Pick or write the line the greeting says, or let it rotate through your own favourites

sideways.idea: An opening for the offline brain
sideways.why: When there's no signal, a distinct short film that says 'working offline' and shows what still works
sideways.builds_on: The film's offline line and the offline brain

cross.idea: The film's search locks on the next thing in your plan
cross.why: The opening ends pointing at what you should do first today

cross.idea: The film greets you in your recognised voice's style
cross.why: The greeting and the score follow the colour you named plainly, and the voice the phone knows is yours (a convenience, never a lock)
An optional look where the opening plays as three comic panels drawn in your style

cross.idea: The film opens on God's Eye
cross.why: In the Eye look, the opening's last shot lands on your own cameras' wall, with layers that never overlap

cross.idea: A boot that starts a lesson
cross.why: On study days the landing opens straight to the next lesson, with the course's progress in the stamp

cross.idea: The film's lock-in tied to the Lens
cross.why: Opening Ghosty from the Lens shortcut plays a one-second lock-in and goes straight to the camera
